metadata.title: perf: eager load EmailTeam relationship in Tool model
metadata.author: jonpspri

description:
## Summary

- Add `email_team` relationship with `lazy="joined"` to `Tool` model for eager loading team names via JOIN
- Add `team` property to `Tool` class that returns team name from the relationship
- Remove manual `_get_team_name` helper and batch loading patterns in `tool_service.py`
- Eliminates N+1 query patterns when fetching tools with team information

## Changes

**mcpgateway/db.py:**
- Added `email_team` relationship with `lazy="joined"` to `Tool` class
- Added `team` property that returns `self.email_team.name if self.email_team else None`

**mcpgateway/services/tool_service.py:**
- Removed `_get_team_name` method
- Removed manual `team_map` batch loading in `list_tools`
- Removed manual `outerjoin`/`add_columns` for team names in `list_server_tools` and `list_tools_for_user`
- Removed unused `EmailTeam` import

**tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_tool_service.py:**
- Added `tool.team = None` to mock fixture
- Updated tests to use `.scalars().all()` pattern
- Fixed flake8 issues (unused imports/variables, inline comments)

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
The eager-loaded `email_team` relationship doesn't filter for active teams. Throughout the codebase, team lookups consistently filter for `EmailTeam.is_active.is_(True)`. The relationship should include a condition to only load active teams to maintain consistency with the previous behavior and other parts of the codebase.

Consider adding a `primaryjoin` condition that includes the `is_active` filter, or document if inactive teams should intentionally be shown.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body:
Using `lazy="joined"` on the relationship causes the EmailTeam table to be joined on every Tool query, even when the team information is not needed. This could impact performance for operations like delete, update, or activate where only the Tool data is required.

Consider using `lazy="selectin"` or leaving the default lazy loading and using `joinedload(DbTool.email_team)` explicitly in queries where team data is needed. This approach provides better control and only loads related data when necessary.
```suggestion
    # Relationship for loading team names; use selectin to avoid unconditional JOINs
    email_team: Mapped[Optional["EmailTeam"]] = relationship("EmailTeam", foreign_keys=[team_id], lazy="selectin")
```

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The Tool class docstring should document the new `team` property that returns the team name from the eagerly-loaded `email_team` relationship. This helps developers understand the available computed properties on the model.

commits.message:
perf: eager load EmailTeam relationship in Tool model to eliminate N+1 queries

Add email_team relationship with lazy="joined" to Tool model, replacing
manual team name lookups with a single JOIN query. This eliminates N+1
query patterns when fetching tools with their team names.

Changes:
- Add email_team relationship to Tool class with lazy="joined"
- Add primaryjoin condition to filter only active teams (is_active == True)
- Add team property to Tool class for convenient team name access
- Document the team property in Tool class docstring
- Remove _get_team_name helper method from tool_service.py
- Remove manual team_map batch loading in list_tools
- Remove manual outerjoin/add_columns in list_server_tools and list_tools_for_user
- Update tests to use new query pattern (.scalars().all())
- Fix flake8 issues in test file
